item.text:
I would harden these parts next:

- [test/orders.js:18-20](test/orders.js#L18) `averageItemPrice` should guard against `items.length === 0`. As written, an empty order gives a divide-by-zero result (`NaN`/`Infinity`), which is a bad default for downstream code.
- [test/orders.js:18-20](test/orders.js#L18) The name is misleading. It returns `calcTotal(items) / items.length`, which is a quantity-weighted average, not the average unit price. If that’s intentional, rename it; if not, compute the mean of `item.price`.
- [test/orders.js:11-15](test/orders.js#L11) `applyDiscount` should validate `total` and `code` more explicitly. Right now unknown codes silently pass through, which is fine if intended, but it also accepts non-string or malformed codes without complaint.
- [test/orders.js:23-26](test/orders.js#L23) `formatOrder` should tolerate missing or malformed `order.items` / `order.discountCode` and either fail fast with a clear error or normalize input. Today a bad shape will throw deep inside `.map()` or `calcTotal()`.
- [test/orders.js:3-8](test/orders.js#L3) `calcTotal` should validate each item has numeric `price` and `qty`. Otherwise a single bad record can turn the whole total into `NaN`.
- [test/orders.js:3-8](test/orders.js#L3) If this module handles money, it should avoid raw floating-point math for currency totals. Using integer cents or a decimal library would prevent rounding drift.
- [test/orders.js:23-26](test/orders.js#L23) `total.toFixed(2)` forces display formatting, which is fine for output, but it means `formatOrder` is mixing presentation with business logic. If you expect reuse, separate formatted display from numeric order computation.

If you want, I can turn that into a minimal hardening patch list ordered by risk.
